subject: Lakeside: service event summary, timeline, and validation schedule
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex@lakeside.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [URGENT] Increased token latency and 502s during peak window

Mina,

We started seeing a spike in 5xx responses and token latencies around 08:40 PDT this morning that impacted our payment auth path. Errors cleared for most traffic by 09:05 but we observed slow tails until ~09:30. Our engineering team saw retries and a couple of customer chargebacks as a direct result.

Can you share what happened, what root cause you’re tracking, and what actions Redwood is taking? We need enough detail for our risk and compliance teams for an internal post-incident review. Also, please confirm whether any payloads or tokens were persisted beyond what our contract allows.

Thanks,
Alex Turner
Head of Integrations, Lakeside Payments
---
Lakeside: support@lakeside.com
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex@lakeside.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [URGENT] Increased token latency and 502s during peak window

Alex — thank you for the report and I’m sorry for the disruption this morning. We’ve opened a dedicated incident channel and our on-call team is investigating. Quick summary:

- A degraded kernel scheduling path interacting with a particular model shard caused delayed KV-cache evictions under burst load, increasing per-token latency and in some cases exceeding our request timeout path which returned 502s.
- No customer data was written to persistent storage outside established audit controls; we see only ephemeral cache activity. We will provide the full timeline and logs.

Immediate actions we took (already applied):
- Rolled a targeted runtime patch to avoid the problematic scheduler path (08:55 PDT).
- Temporarily raised request timeout limits for affected routes while we validated stability.
- Enabled a fallback to a compatible model variant for high-priority traffic to prevent further user-facing errors.

I’ll follow up with a concise RCA and an evidence package for your compliance team by EOD. If you need an interim call today, I’m available 11:00–12:00 PDT.

— Mina Haddad
Senior Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Lakeside: service event summary, timeline, and validation schedule

Team — forwarding Lakeside’s ask. Quick notes:

- Impact window: 08:40–09:30 PDT; primary customer-facing symptoms were elevated p95/p99 token latency and intermittent 502s on the inference gateway.
- Suspect component: runtime scheduler + KV eviction interaction under a specific shard layout. Rafael, please confirm the kernel-level mitigation we applied and whether the rollback we did at 08:55 is safe to keep as a permanent config.
- Evidence we need to attach to customer: sampled logs (gateway and runtime), timeline of operator actions, and the patch diff + test results.

Let’s keep external communication tightly scoped — timeline, root cause hypothesis, corrective actions already taken, next steps, and a validation schedule. Marissa — can you propose the wording for the customer-facing RCA? David — please pull the sampled logs and redact any sensitive fields (PII/token values). I’ll assemble the package and send the brief by EOD.

Thanks,
Mina
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex@lakeside.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 17:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Lakeside: incident transparency brief, timeline, and validation schedule

Alex — following up with the customer brief and attachments (attached: RCA timeline PDF, sampled logs). High-level summary below; full package available on the Drive link included.

Executive summary:
- What happened: During a morning peak on 2027-03-12 we observed an interaction between our runtime scheduler and KV-cache eviction on a subset of model shards that caused queueing and elevated token latencies. When request processing exceeded configured timeouts, the gateway returned 502 responses for a subset of requests.
- Scope of impact: a small fraction of requests routed to the affected shard layout experienced errors and latency spikes between 08:40–09:30 PDT. We estimate Lakeside’s traffic saw a 0.9% error increase and a 13% p99 latency lift during the window (sampled metrics attached).
- Data exposure: None. All cache state was ephemeral and no customer payloads were persisted outside normal retention; logs we’ve attached have been redacted for tokens/PII.

Timeline (high level):
- 08:39 PDT — alerting: gateway p95/p99 and 502 counts spike.
- 08:43 PDT — on-call acknowledged and began triage; initial mitigation to increase gateway timeouts and divert high-priority routes.
- 08:52 PDT — runtime patch deployed; step-back to ensure stability.
- 08:55 PDT — targeted rollback of problematic scheduler path and activation of fallback model variant for susceptible traffic.
- 09:05 PDT — 502 counts returned to baseline; latency tail receded over the following 25 minutes.

What we changed (corrective actions):
- Deployed a runtime fix to decouple eviction-driven wakeups from the scheduler path (patch included).
- Added a short-term traffic steering rule to avoid the specific shard layout during high-burst windows.
- Implemented enhanced observability: new counters and tracing spans around eviction events to catch recurrence earlier.
- Scheduled a follow-on change: a small rebalancing of shard placement logic to reduce contention risk (sprint target: 4 weeks).

Customer remediation & validation plan:
- Today: delivered evidence package (attached) and a summary for your compliance team.
- This week: we will run a joint validation window with Lakeside to replay a representative burst in our staging mirror. Proposed dates: Wed 2027-03-17 or Thu 2027-03-18 09:00–10:30 PDT. Please confirm availability.
- Within 30 days: shard rebalancing rollout in a canary-first approach with predefined rollback criteria.

Offer of account-level remediation: we recognize the impact this had on your payment flows. As a gesture, Redwood will apply a one-time credit to Lakeside’s March usage invoice covering estimated incremental costs tied to retries and operational overhead. We’ll share the credit calculation and require your acceptance to apply it.

Attached: 20270315-lakeside-rca-timeline.pdf, 20270315-system-logs-sampled.txt (redacted). Full evidence and diffs: https://drive.redwood.com/teams/mina/lakeside-rca/2027-03-15

If you want a walkthrough of the attached timeline and logs, I can set up a technical readout with Rafael and David tomorrow. Thank you again for the heads-up and for your patience while we resolved this.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
